thesis: Victoria's Secret's confirmed Q2 result supports a long: net sales rose 10%, comparable sales rose 9%, and the company raised full-year sales and company-defined adjusted operating-income guidance. The strongest counter-evidence is the sharp post-result price decline, ongoing tariff uncertainty, and third-quarter operating-income guidance of only $10 million to $20 million; those do not change the read because the reported quarter's broad sales growth and raised full-year outlook are company-specific and already disclosed rather than speculative.
invalidation: A subsequent company filing cuts fiscal-2026 sales or adjusted operating-income guidance, or comparable sales turn negative.

thesis: Arch Capital's volume spike does not have a fresh company-disclosed catalyst, so avoid. The latest filed quarter shows book value per share rose 2.8%, but quarterly net income declined to $1.047 billion from $1.227 billion and annualized operating return on equity declined to 15.3% from 18.2%; this mixed, older evidence does not justify treating today's volume as fundamental confirmation.
invalidation: A new company filing discloses a specific catalyst with improving underwriting profitability and book-value growth.

thesis: Zscaler's confirmed fiscal-2026 fourth-quarter result supports a long: quarterly revenue and annual recurring revenue each rose 25%, operating loss narrowed, and management reported a record 24% company-defined adjusted operating margin. The strongest counter-evidence is free-cash-flow margin falling to 7% from 24%, slower fiscal-2027 growth guidance, and a disclosed 3% workforce reduction; those do not change the read because operating cash remained positive and the realized growth, margin, and sales-productivity evidence is company-specific, while the cash-flow decline was tied to elevated capital expenditure and internal-use software.
invalidation: A subsequent filing shows annual-recurring-revenue growth below management's fiscal-2027 range, renewed sales-execution deterioration, or cash generation failing to recover after the disclosed investment cycle.
sources: Zscaler Q4 and FY2026 results: https://ir.zscaler.com/node/16456

thesis: Samsara's confirmed fiscal-2027 second-quarter result supports a long: revenue and annual recurring revenue each grew 30%, reported operating income turned positive at $4.9 million, and free cash flow rose to $64.7 million. The strongest counter-evidence is $101.1 million of stock-based compensation and the pending Federal Circuit appeal from the Motive dispute; those do not change the read because the quarter produced positive operating income and cash flow, while the legal search identified no scheduled ruling, hearing, trial, or compliance deadline within the next roughly 90 days.
invalidation: A subsequent company filing reverses operating profitability, materially slows annual-recurring-revenue growth, or discloses a scheduled adverse legal event before the next review.

thesis: Netskope's confirmed fiscal-2027 second-quarter result supports a long: revenue rose 29%, annual recurring revenue rose 27%, gross margin expanded, and the company ended the quarter with $1.1 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. The strongest counter-evidence is an $89.8 million operating loss and $29.8 million of negative free cash flow, both worse in absolute terms; those do not change the read because the company-defined adjusted operating loss narrowed substantially, growth remained near 30%, and disclosed liquidity covers the present burn.
invalidation: A subsequent filing shows annual-recurring-revenue or revenue growth decelerating sharply without operating-loss or cash-flow improvement, or liquidity falls materially.
sources: Justia Netskope v. Fortinet docket order: https://cases.justia.com/federal/district-courts/california/candce/4%3A2025cv02360/446034/168/0.pdf
